rows.stem: An iron nail is placed in a solution of copper sulphate. The nail is taken out after 15 minutes. The nail will be found to be covered with :
rows.solution:
Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper from copper sulphate solution:

\(\mathrm{Fe(s) + CuSO_4(aq) \rightarrow FeSO_4(aq) + Cu(s)}\)

The copper set free deposits on the nail as a brown (reddish-brown) coating, and the blue colour of the solution fades.

This is option (B) brown deposit.

rows.stem: Which of the following reactions is an endothermic reaction ?

options.label: B
options.text: Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost

options.label: D
options.text: Decomposition of calcium carbonate to form quick lime and carbon dioxide.

rows.solution:
An endothermic reaction absorbs energy. Calcium carbonate decomposes into quick lime and carbon dioxide only when heat is supplied:

\(\mathrm{CaCO_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} CaO(s) + CO_2(g)}\)

Burning of coal, decomposition of vegetable matter into compost, and respiration all give out energy, so they are exothermic.

This is option (D) Decomposition of calcium carbonate to form quick lime and carbon dioxide.

rows.stem: In the given diagram the leaf shown belongs to which plant ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the plant is identified only from the boxed drawing of a leaf with small plantlets growing from notches along its margin, labelled 'Adventious buds' (sic); the stem names nothing, and naming the plant here would state the answer. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
The leaf in the drawing has small plantlets growing from the buds in the notches along its margin. This is the leaf of Bryophyllum, which reproduces vegetatively in this way: each bud, on falling on soil, can grow into a new plant.

This is option (D) Bryophyllum.

rows.stem: The speed of light in vacuum is \(3 \times 10^8\) m/s. If the speed of light in a medium is \(2.25 \times 10^8\) m/s, the absolute refractive index of the medium is :
rows.solution:
The absolute refractive index of a medium is the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in the medium:

\(n_m = \dfrac{c}{v} = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{2.25 \times 10^8} = \dfrac{300}{225} = \dfrac{4}{3}\).

This is option (C) \(\dfrac{4}{3}\).

rows.stem:
Study the following statements :

(a) A fuse in a circuit prevents damage to the circuit due to overloading.

(b) Total resistance in a circuit increases due to overloading.

(c) During short circuiting the current in the circuit abruptly increases.

(d) In order that each appliance has same current, they are connected in parallel to each other.

The correct statements are
rows.solution:
(a) A fuse melts when the current becomes too large, so it prevents damage to the circuit due to overloading: true.

(b) Overloading means too many appliances are connected (in parallel) to one socket, which lowers the total resistance and so raises the current. The total resistance decreases, not increases: false.

(c) In a short circuit the live and neutral wires come into direct contact, the resistance becomes very small and the current increases abruptly: true.

(d) Appliances are connected in parallel so that each gets the same potential difference (the full supply voltage), not the same current; each draws a current according to its own resistance: false.

So statements (a) and (c) are the correct ones. This is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Carbon reduces the oxides of Sodium and Magnesium.

**Reason (R) :** Sodium and Magnesium have more affinity for Oxygen than Carbon.
rows.context: These questions consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
Sodium and magnesium are high up in the activity series, and carbon cannot reduce their oxides; these metals are obtained by electrolysis of their molten chlorides. The Assertion is false.

Sodium and magnesium have a greater affinity for oxygen than carbon has, which is exactly why carbon cannot take the oxygen away from them. The Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The colour of clear sky appears blue.

**Reason (R) :** Light of blue colour has longer wavelength as compared to the light of red colour so it is scattered more in the upper atmosphere.
rows.context: These questions consist of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

rows.solution:
The clear sky appears blue because the fine particles in the atmosphere scatter blue light, of shorter wavelength, much more strongly than red light. The Assertion is true.

Blue light has a shorter wavelength than red light, not a longer one, so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
Give one example of each of the following :

(i) Chemical reaction showing evolution of gas.

(ii) Change in the colour of the substance during a chemical reaction.
rows.solution:
(i) Evolution of a gas: zinc granules react with dilute sulphuric acid and hydrogen gas is given off.

\(\mathrm{Zn(s) + H_2SO_4(aq) \rightarrow ZnSO_4(aq) + H_2(g)}\)

(ii) Change in colour: when copper powder is heated in air, the reddish-brown copper turns black because copper oxide forms.

\(\mathrm{2Cu(s) + O_2(g) \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2CuO(s)}\)

(Any other suitable example of each is also correct.)

rows.stem:
Translate the following statements into chemical equations and then balance them :

(i) Hydrogen sulphide gas burns in air to give water and sulphur dioxide.

(ii) Silver bromide on exposure to sunlight decomposes into silver and bromine.
rows.solution:
(i) Hydrogen sulphide burns in oxygen to give sulphur dioxide and water:

\(\mathrm{2H_2S(g) + 3O_2(g) \rightarrow 2SO_2(g) + 2H_2O(l)}\)

Check: 4 H, 2 S and 6 O on each side.

(ii) Silver bromide decomposes in sunlight into silver and bromine:

\(\mathrm{2AgBr(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Br_2(g)}\)

Check: 2 Ag and 2 Br on each side. The marking scheme deducts half a mark for each equation left unbalanced.

rows.stem: Name the blood vessel which brings blood to the kidneys. Why is nephron called a basic filtration unit of kidney ? Write the role of tubular part of nephron in urine formation.
rows.solution:
The renal artery brings blood to the kidneys.

The nephron is called the basic filtration unit because each kidney is made of a large number of nephrons, and in each one the blood is filtered and the nitrogenous wastes, such as urea and uric acid, are removed from it.

Role of the tubular part: as the initial filtrate passes along the tubule, useful substances such as glucose, amino acids, salts and much of the water are selectively reabsorbed into the blood, so that only the waste is left as urine.

rows.stem: Mendel crossed a round and yellow seeded pea plant with a wrinkled and green seeded pea plant. What did the plants of \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation look like in terms of shape and colour of seed ? On self-pollinating \(\mathrm{F_1}\) generation plants, plants with four types of combinations of characters were seen in \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation. Write the combinations along with their ratios.
rows.solution:
All the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants had round and yellow seeds: round is dominant over wrinkled, and yellow over green.

On self-pollinating the \(\mathrm{F_1}\) plants, the \(\mathrm{F_2}\) generation showed four combinations of characters:

Round and yellow: 9

Round and green: 3

Wrinkled and yellow: 3

Wrinkled and green: 1

That is, the ratio \(9 : 3 : 3 : 1\).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: A person suffering from an eye defect uses lenses of power \(-1\) D. Name the defect of vision and list its two causes. State the nature (converging/diverging) of the corrective lens.
rows.solution:
A lens of power \(-1\) D is a concave lens, of focal length \(f = \dfrac{1}{P} = -1\) m. Such a lens corrects myopia (near-sightedness).

Two causes of myopia:

1. Excessive curvature of the eye lens.

2. Elongation of the eyeball.

The corrective lens is diverging.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: What is presbyopia ? Name the type of lenses used for the correction of this defect. State the nature (converging/diverging) of the upper part of such lenses.
rows.solution:
Presbyopia is the defect in which the power of accommodation of the eye usually decreases with ageing, so the person finds it difficult to see nearby objects comfortably and distinctly. It happens because the ciliary muscles gradually weaken and the eye lens loses its flexibility.

It is corrected with a convex lens; a person who suffers from both myopia and hypermetropia needs bifocal lenses.

In a bifocal lens the upper part is a concave lens, so it is diverging (it helps in seeing distant objects), while the lower part is a convex, converging lens for reading.

rows.stem:
(a) Sodium metal is stored under kerosene oil. Why ?

(b) Some metal oxides are soluble in water. What are the aqueous solutions of these oxides called ? Write one example of such a solution.

(c) At ordinary temperature the surface of metals such as magnesium, aluminium, zinc etc. is covered with a thin layer. What is the composition of this layer ? State its importance.
rows.solution:
(a) Sodium is so reactive that, kept in the open, it reacts vigorously with the oxygen and moisture of the air and can catch fire. It does not react with kerosene, so it is stored under kerosene oil to keep air and water away from it.

(b) The aqueous solutions of soluble metal oxides are called alkalis. Example: sodium hydroxide solution, formed when sodium oxide dissolves in water (potassium hydroxide is another).

\(\mathrm{Na_2O(s) + H_2O(l) \rightarrow 2NaOH(aq)}\)

(c) The thin layer is the oxide of the metal (for example magnesium oxide on magnesium, aluminium oxide on aluminium). This protective oxide layer prevents the metal underneath from further oxidation (corrosion).

rows.stem:
(a) List any two contraceptive methods practised only by women. Mention how these methods work.

(b) Write the two roles performed by testes in human males.
rows.solution:
(a) Any two methods used only by women:

1. Oral pills (chemical method): they change the hormonal balance of the body so that eggs are not released, and fertilisation cannot take place.

2. Loop or copper-T: a device placed in the uterus to prevent pregnancy. (The marking scheme says it works by checking the entry of sperms through the vagina; it sits inside the uterus, not at the vagina.)

3. Surgical method (blocking the fallopian tubes): the egg cannot reach the uterus, so it cannot meet the sperm and fertilisation is prevented.

(b) Two roles of the testes:

1. Formation of sperms (the male germ cells).

2. Secretion of the hormone testosterone, which regulates the formation of sperms and brings about the changes in appearance seen in boys at puberty.

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: Define the term solenoid. Draw the pattern of magnetic field lines around a current carrying solenoid. State how this magnetic field can be used to magnetise a piece of magnetic material, like soft iron.
rows.solution:
A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns of insulated copper wire wrapped closely in the shape of a cylinder.

Diagram: draw the solenoid connected to a battery and a key. Inside the solenoid draw the field lines as parallel straight lines along its axis; outside, draw them as closed loops going from one end of the solenoid round to the other, like the field of a bar magnet, with the end where the lines leave as the north pole and the end where they enter as the south pole. Mark the direction of the field lines with arrows: the marking scheme deducts half a mark if they are missing.

The field inside the solenoid is strong and uniform. A piece of magnetic material such as soft iron placed inside the coil is magnetised by this field while the current flows, forming an electromagnet.
